summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell degranulation syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, and prior epinephrine-induced MI was admitted for a typical mast cell flare triggered by an upper respiratory infection. She presented with itching, chest tightness, epigastric pain, and vomiting, and was treated with IV Benadryl, Ativan, and oral Dilaudid as needed. Her symptoms resolved overnight. A chest X-ray showed only minimal atelectasis with no acute process, and EKG was unchanged without cardiac ischemia. She was restarted on montelukast, which she had not taken for a month, and discharged home with updated medications and follow-up plans. No procedures were performed.
